sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Glen Ellyn, Illinois?
sections.html:
The quickest route in Glen Ellyn is an as-is sale to a buyer who does not need a mortgage or a long inspection period, though a well-prepared listing can also close on a firm schedule. What slows most Glen Ellyn closings is not the buyer but the village paperwork: the transfer stamp, the clearwater inspection and the final water reading.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you want to test the market for the highest price.
  • Sell privately if you are comfortable handling contracts and disclosures on your own.
  • Sell as-is for cash when the house has deferred repairs, an estate attached to it, or a closing date that cannot slip.

Glen Ellyn is a village in DuPage County about 24 miles due west of downtown Chicago, in Milton Township. With a Metra station downtown, three school districts and a village sump pump rule, train access, school boundaries and basement drainage are the topics to prepare before you talk to buyers.

sections.h2: What does the Glen Ellyn housing market look like?
sections.html:
Glen Ellyn is a high-value, owner-occupied suburb: the Census Bureau puts its July 1, 2025 population estimate at 28,750, compared with 28,846 counted in 2020. For 2020 to 2024 it lists the median value of owner-occupied housing at $544,000, an owner-occupied rate of 78.3 percent, and 10,698 households.

Median household income over that period was $140,938, median gross rent was $1,433, and 68.2 percent of adults 25 and older held a bachelor's degree or higher. Mean travel time to work was 29.1 minutes, which fits a village whose commuters ride the train or drive to Chicago and the western suburbs.

College of DuPage has its main campus here and was the largest employer on the village's 2021 financial report with 3,837 employees. School District 41 listed 549 employees and School District 87 listed 485.

The area began as Babcock's Grove after two brothers staked claims near the East Branch of the DuPage River in 1833. The Galena and Chicago Union Railroad finished its line through the village in 1849, and the center of the community shifted to the area around the depot.

sections.h2: Which schools, trains and parks draw buyers to Glen Ellyn?
sections.html:
School district is the first fact to confirm for any Glen Ellyn address. Primary schools are part of Glen Ellyn School District 41 and Community Consolidated School District 89, and high school students attend Glenbard Township High School District 87.

Elementary schools in the village include Abraham Lincoln, Arbor View, Benjamin Franklin, Churchill, Forest Glen, Park View and Westfield, and Glen Crest Middle School and Hadley Junior High serve older grades. Confirm which school serves your address with the district, since district boundaries do not follow village lines everywhere.

Transportation is a second selling point. The Metra Union Pacific West Line stops at the Glen Ellyn station at 551 Crescent Boulevard, about 22.4 miles from Ogilvie Transportation Center. Pace routes 714, 715 and 301 run along Roosevelt Road, and Roosevelt Road also leads to Interstate 355 at the east end of the village.

The Glen Ellyn Park District, set up in 1919, maintains 30 parks and two lakes, and the Illinois Prairie Path bike trail runs through the village. Lake Ellyn was created in the late 1800s when a dam was built on a nearby stream.

sections.h2: How does the Glen Ellyn transfer stamp and clearwater inspection work?
sections.html:
The Village of Glen Ellyn charges a real estate transfer stamp of $3 for each $1,000 of property sales price, and the home seller pays it. The stamp is required to record the deed, and the village will not issue it until every inspection is passed and every fee is paid.

Glen Ellyn steps before a transfer stamp is issued (Village of Glen Ellyn)
StepWho handles itContact
Transfer stamp application, completed onlineVillage of Glen EllynOnline form
Clearwater inspectionPublic Works630-469-6756, choose clearwater appointments
Final water readingUtility Billing630-547-5235
Stamp tax of $3 per $1,000 of sales pricePaid by the sellerVillage

The clearwater inspection comes from Village Code 3-42-15. It is required any time a stamp is needed, including a sale, a title transfer, putting a deed into a trust or a refinance, and it applies to exempt transactions too. The inspector checks whether the building has a sump pump and whether the pump is illegally tied into the sanitary sewer.

The rule exists because rainwater in the sanitary system can overload it during a major storm and push sewage back into homes. Village Code 7-9-25 bars clearwater from sanitary sewers, and Code 8-1-10 bars directing sump pump, gutter or similar discharge into the public right-of-way. If the inspector finds a problem, fix it before closing. Public Works can explain acceptable options, which may include moving the discharge point or connecting to the storm sewer.

Some sellers may qualify for a refund of the transfer tax. The eligibility rules are on the village's refund application, so ask the village before assuming one applies.

sections.h2: What permits and contractor rules apply to a Glen Ellyn house?
sections.html:
Permit work in Glen Ellyn goes through the village's online permit system, and open work can complicate a sale. The Building Division reviews plans, issues permits, inspects construction and enforces the building, property maintenance, fire and zoning codes.

Applications are signed electronically with the owner's authorization, and supporting documents such as plans, a plat of survey and contracts are uploaded with them. Construction plans must be prepared and stamped by an Illinois registered design professional. Fees depend on the project type and construction cost, and refundable deposits cover possible damage to public property. All contractors must meet the license and insurance requirements in Village Code Section 4-1-11, and a contractor working in violation can be cited or have a stop work order issued.

  • Locate permit records and final inspection sign-offs for decks, additions and finished basements.
  • Ask Public Works about drainage if your lot has a history of standing water.
  • Keep a copy of your plat of survey, since many permit and closing steps ask for it.

Selling as-is to a cash buyer puts the cleanup of open permits on the buyer, as long as the contract spells out who takes on what.

sections.h2: How do DuPage County property taxes work for Glen Ellyn sellers?
sections.html:
DuPage County mails one tax bill a year with two coupons, and the 2025 taxes were due June 1 and September 1, 2026. Late payments carry interest of 1.5 percent per month under state law, and the postmark decides whether a payment was on time.

Township assessors set the starting assessed value, and the law requires assessments at one-third of fair market value. To appeal, first review your property record with the township assessor. Appeals go to the DuPage County Board of Review and must be filed within 30 days after the township assessment roll is published. The county asks for three or more comparable properties as evidence, and written decisions typically arrive the following March. A further appeal can go to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

The residential exemption depends on living in the home by January 1 of the tax year, and the township assessor starts it, so new owners should contact that office after moving in. The senior assessment freeze carries a household income limit of $65,000. Call the DuPage Supervisor of Assessments at 630-407-5858 or the Treasurer at 630-407-5900 to confirm your parcel.

faqs.q: Who pays the Glen Ellyn transfer stamp?
faqs.a: The home seller pays it. The village sets the rate at $3 for each $1,000 of sales price, and the stamp is issued only after the clearwater inspection is passed and all fees are paid.

faqs.q: What is a clearwater inspection in Glen Ellyn?
faqs.a: It is a village check for a sump pump and for any illegal sump connection to the sanitary sewer. Village Code 3-42-15 requires it when a transfer stamp is needed, and you schedule it with Public Works at 630-469-6756.

faqs.q: How do I schedule the final water reading in Glen Ellyn?
faqs.a: Call the Utility Billing Department at 630-547-5235. The village asks you to schedule it after you complete the online transfer stamp application, and the reading and the clearwater inspection both come before the stamp.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Glen Ellyn house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, apart from anything the village requires for the stamp, such as correcting an illegal clearwater connection. Cosmetic and mechanical repairs are negotiable in an as-is sale and are priced into the offer.

faqs.q: When are DuPage County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For the 2025 taxes, the installments were due June 1 and September 1, 2026. Late payments add 1.5 percent per month, and your bill shows the dates for later years.
